clue.text: Former slaves rush miles into marshland

indicators.note: into says the rush and miles go inside the marshland word

parts.note: a fen is low marshy land
a reed is a rush, the waterside plant

explanation.surface: Escaped slaves hurry for miles into a swamp.
explanation.definitionFit: Freed slaves were historically called by this term, meaning people released from slavery.

clue.text: Foreign money is to preserve order

parts.note: the franc was the currency of France and other countries
taken as written
to can food is to preserve it in tins

explanation.surface: Foreign cash is kept to keep things orderly.
explanation.definitionFit: A friar of the religious order founded by St Francis of Assisi is called by this name.

clue.text: Left over big picture being off course

parts.note: extra means surplus, left over
a mural is a large painting on a wall

explanation.surface: A big leftover painting is off course, wandering astray.
explanation.definitionFit: Extramural study lies outside a university's regular courses, so it is off the normal course.

clue.text: Who's foe is held back by joke ladder?

indicators.note: held back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A Doctor Who enemy is restrained by a novelty ladder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Who' is Doctor Who, the BBC science-fiction series. The run KELAD spans 'joKE LADder', and 'held back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: The Daleks are the best-known enemies of the Doctor in the TV series Doctor Who.

clue.text: Tentative mixture — for example nitre

indicators.note: a mixture tells us the letters of the following words are blended into a new order

explanation.surface: A chemist's trial blend uses nitre as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' looks like part of 'for example', but EXAMPLE alone is fodder with NITRE.
explanation.definitionFit: An experimental approach is a trial one, tentative and not yet settled.

clue.text: Headings involve copywriter

annotationWithheld.why: Headings involve copywriter (6): S and E (compass headings) around CRIB (copy) gives SCRIBE, but 'copywriter' must give both CRIB and the definition, one word doing two jobs

clue.text: Little Bird was a remarkable Native American

parts.note: a chick is a young bird

indicators.note: remarkable read as re-markable, able to be marked out afresh, signals the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Native American called Little Bird was a remarkable figure.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chickasaw are a Native American people originally from the south-eastern United States.

clue.text: Press home or is held back

indicators.note: is held says one piece is gripped inside another

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: back tells us the word or is read the other way round

explanation.surface: Push home, or else it is restrained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'home' looks part of the pressing picture but gives its usual crossword sense of 'in'; 'back' and 'is held' are the two indicators.
explanation.definitionFit: To iron clothes is to press them smooth with a heated appliance.

clue.text: Deserve to get vessel delivered

indicators.note: delivered in the sense of spoken or uttered signals a word said out loud

parts.note: an urn is a vase-like vessel

explanation.surface: A pot arrives and one deserves to receive it.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn something is to merit or deserve it through one's efforts.

clue.text: Open late to make a quick buck

indicators.note: to make says the letters are used to form something new, rearranged

explanation.surface: Trading after hours earns easy money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a quick buck' looks like easy money but is a fast-running male animal.
explanation.definitionFit: An antelope is a swift deer-like animal, and a male one is called a buck.

clue.text: Arrangement of us in severity

parts.note: a rig is an arrangement of equipment, as on a ship
our means belonging to us

explanation.surface: Our set-up is a strict one.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigour means strictness or harshness, a synonym of severity.

clue.text: Swimmer requesting quiet when breaking cover for trunks

indicators.note: breaking means splitting the cover open to hold the other pieces

parts.note: bark is the covering of tree trunks
asking is requesting
sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: A swimmer asks for silence while hiding his bathing trunks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trunks' suggests swimwear but means tree trunks, which bark covers.
explanation.definitionFit: The basking shark is a huge plankton-feeding fish, a swimmer of the open sea.

clue.text: Biscuit with salt as topping

parts.note: a cracker is a thin crisp biscuit
salt and jack are both old slang for a sailor

explanation.surface: A savoury biscuit with salt sprinkled on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topping' looks like a garnish but is old British slang for excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Crackerjack is slang for something first-rate, as topping is an old word for excellent.

clue.text: Palmer's trek does brim over with awful years

indicators.note: over says the word for brim is turned upside down in this down entry

parts.note: a lip is a rim or brim
grim means awful
an age is many years

explanation.surface: Deer cross a hat brim over terrible years of travel.
explanation.walkthrough: A palmer was a medieval pilgrim who carried a palm leaf from the Holy Land. 'over' turns LIP into PIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A palmer was a pilgrim, and a pilgrim's long journey to a shrine is this.

clue.text: Rudely looked over talent that's caught going bare

indicators.note: over means the first word is placed around the second

parts.note: to stare is to look rudely

indicators.note: going says the caught letter departs from the talent word

parts.note: a knack is a talent
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone eyed a talented streaker running about bare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught' looks like being caught naked, but it names the letter that 'going' removes; 'over' wraps the rude look round what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Stark naked means completely bare, without a stitch of clothing.

clue.text: Taken in time to enter dynasty

indicators.note: to enter says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the Sung (Song) dynasty ruled China

explanation.surface: Absorbed in time into a ruling dynasty.
explanation.definitionFit: To be stung is to be cheated or swindled, as when taken in by a con.

clue.text: A cottager that makes clothing

indicators.note: that makes says the letters of the words before it are formed into something new

explanation.surface: A rural cottager makes garments.
explanation.definitionFit: A greatcoat is a heavy overcoat, an item of clothing.

clue.text: Temporary fashion garment

parts.note: to fashion is to make
a shift is a simple dress

explanation.surface: A stopgap fashion garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Makeshift describes something improvised for the time being, temporary.

clue.text: Warrior king not known to capture brave male

indicators.note: to capture means the outer word holds the others

parts.note: anon is short for anonymous, not known by name
game means plucky, brave

explanation.surface: An anonymous warrior king captures a brave man.
explanation.definitionFit: Agamemnon was the king of Mycenae who led the Greeks in the Trojan War.

clue.text: The hazard of New Age remedies

indicators.note: of says the letters come from within the words that follow

explanation.surface: The risk involved in alternative New Age cures.
explanation.definitionFit: A hazard is an old word for a bet or stake, like a gamble.

clue.text: Answer is in drawing trade

indicators.note: in says the answer abbreviation goes inside the drawing word

parts.note: traction is the act of drawing or pulling

explanation.surface: The answer lies in pulling off a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A transaction is a business deal, an act of trade.

clue.text: Pass on currency

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
taken as written

explanation.surface: Hand on money.
explanation.definitionFit: The colon is the currency unit of Costa Rica and formerly El Salvador.

clue.text: Feet up for a change …

indicators.note: up in a down entry means the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: paws are animals' feet

explanation.surface: Putting your feet up for a change.
explanation.definitionFit: A swap is an exchange, one thing given for another, a change.

clue.text: … legs up for a bit

indicators.note: up in a down entry means the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: pins is slang for legs

explanation.surface: Legs raised for a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A snip is a small cut piece, a bit.

clue.text: Separate airily to gain present

parts.note: to win is to gain
now is the present moment

explanation.surface: Breezily divide things up to get a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: To winnow is to separate grain from chaff by blowing air through it.

clue.text: Entrance money that was sign of quality

parts.note: a hall is an entrance passage
the mark was the German currency

explanation.surface: Lobby cash that marked something fine.
explanation.definitionFit: A hallmark is a stamp on precious metal, and by extension a distinguishing mark of quality.

clue.text: Young one consumed grub to do this

parts.note: a pup is a young animal
ate means consumed

explanation.surface: A young animal ate a grub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grub' looks like food the pup ate, but it is the larva, which turns into a chrysalis.
explanation.definitionFit: A grub, or larva, goes through this stage when it becomes a pupa.

clue.text: Severely distressed person?

parts.note: read distressed as de-tressed, with all tresses removed, and severely as a severe close crop of the hair

explanation.definitionFit: A skinhead has a shaven or closely cropped head, all locks removed.
